description: **Early exit, output writers, and signals.** `strictcli.ExitNow(code, message)` ends a command from anywhere in its call stack through the exit step: deferred functions run, the command exits `code`, and the message is printed as `error: <message>` (under `--json`, the last error diagnostic); `strictcli.Go(ctx, fn)` runs a goroutine whose `ExitNow` or panic is delivered to the handler, `App.Call` returns `*strictcli.ExitError`, and MCP answers `exit code <code>: <message>`. `ctx.Out(text)` writes the command's answer and is never hidden by `--quiet`; `PayloadRenderer(fn)` declares a human rendering of the payload; `ctx.Document()` writes an `OwnsStdout()` command's document. `App.Run` catches SIGINT and SIGTERM while the handler runs and closes `ctx.Done()`; when the handler returns, the command exits 130 or 143 with `error: canceled by signal <SIGNAL>`, and a second signal gets the default action.

**The `--json` document is `interface_version` 3, stdout is guarded under `--json`, and warnings and errors are prefixed.** The document carries an `output` member after `payload` (the text `ctx.Out` wrote plus captured child stdout, `null` when none); a child run through `Spawn` or `Run(Stream(true))` under `--json` no longer writes beside it. While a handler runs in machine mode, file descriptor 1 is redirected, and any byte written outside the framework (`fmt.Println`, `os.Stdout`, an unmanaged child) fails the run with exit 1 unless the code is already nonzero, plus the error diagnostic `stdout written outside the framework: <n> bytes: "<excerpt>"`. In human mode `ctx.Warn` prints `warning: <message>` and `ctx.Error` prints `error: <message>`.

**--lint-framework-use.** Every app reserves `--lint-framework-use`, which scans the program run from its module root (every strictcli main package and the module packages it imports, resolving import aliases) for process exits, direct stdout and stderr writes, argv access, environment reads, and `strictcli.ExitNow` inside a raw `go` func literal, and exits 1 listing each finding as `<path>:<line>: <rule>: <message>`.

Under `--json` the runtime guard now redirects stdout at the operating-system level on every Unix (including Solaris, illumos, and AIX) and on Windows, so a direct write to the standard output or a child started outside the effects handle is caught there too. The module now requires `golang.org/x/sys`.

A child started through `ctx.Effects().Spawn` that is still running when its handler ends is now killed (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after one second; at once on Windows) and fails the run: exit 1 unless the status is already nonzero, plus `error: child process <pid> was still running when the handler ended and was killed: <argv>`. The exit step no longer waits for such a child. Wait on every child you spawn, or end it with the new `Spawned.Kill()`; `Spawned.Signal(sig)` sends any signal.
`ExitError` gains `Payload`: what the command supplied through `ctx.Payload` before its early exit, nil when it supplied nothing.

The `config set`, `config init`, and `config edit` commands report their own errors through the error writer: printed once as `error: <message>` and carried as `error` diagnostics under `--json` instead of bare stderr lines; `config init`'s refusal now reads `config init: config file already exists: <path>` as in the other implementations.
Programs built with strictcli compile for targets where `int` is 32 bits wide (`GOARCH=386`, `arm`, `mips`, and `mipsle`) instead of failing with `choiceMaxMagnitude ... overflows int`.

`check --ignore-warnings` and `RunChecksOptions.IgnoreWarnings` are removed: `check` stays the full report and exits nonzero on warnings, and the new `failing-checks` command (same selection flags) is the run where only error-level failures fail. Every `[checks.<name>]` in checks.toml must now declare `description` (one non-empty line) and `subject` (the options subject file its option belongs in: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, never `manifest`); a checks.toml lacking either panics at construction with `checks.toml: check "<name>": missing required field "description"` (or `"subject"`), so add both to every declared check. `--dump-schema` publishes them on each check entry.

**Check values, `failing-checks`, and named hooks.** `app.SetCheckValueResolver(func(name string) (strictcli.CheckValue, bool))` lets an app assign each check a `CheckValue{Value, Source}`: `off` does not run the check (shown as an `OFF` row with its source), `warn` reports its failures as warnings, `error` runs it as registered; a value above the registered severity, outside the three, or without a source is refused. The new `failing-checks` command runs the same selection as `check` and prints only error-level failures, exiting nonzero exactly when one exists. `[hooks.<name>]` tables in checks.toml (`tag = "<expression>"`) name a selection that `check --hook <name>` and `failing-checks --hook <name>` run, and `check --list` shows each check's value and where it came from.
`check --list` on a checks.toml that declares no checks prints `No checks defined.` instead of a bare table header, as the Python and TypeScript implementations do.

Names follow one rule, refused where they are declared: command, group, deprecated-command, and long flag names (at every level, globals and choice scopes included), choice, constraint, tag, check, hook, grant, and update-resource names must be lowercase kebab-case of at least two characters (`[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*`), and a `Short(...)` must be one ASCII letter (uppercase allowed). `help` and `version` are framework command names, refused for any command, group, or deprecated command at any depth. Rename a violating name, for example `StringFlag("m", ..., Short("m"))` to `StringFlag("message", ..., Short("m"))`; positional argument names and the App name are unaffected.

`--dump-schema` is replaced by `<app> help --json`, which prints the help document on stdout (the `--json` document goes to stderr) and writes no file: produce a committed schema with `<app> help --json > .strictcli/schema.json`. `WithSchemaPath` and `WithSchemaPathRelativeToRoot` are removed, `project_id` is now the main module path from the program's build information rather than the `go.mod` in the working directory, and passing `--dump-schema` is refused naming `help --json`. `--help` and `--version` stay text only: with `--json` they are refused naming the command that prints the machine form. The root and group help pages now end with `Use '<app> help <command>' for more information.`
